questions.q: Which four foundational harms does Haidt identify?
a: Social deprivation, sleep loss, attention fragmentation and addiction
Anxiety, depression, isolation and poor grades
Bullying, comparison, boredom and misinformation
Obesity, loneliness, stress and screen fatigue
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists these four as the costs of a phone-based childhood.

questions.q: What is Haidt's central claim about modern childhood?
a: Kids are overprotected offline and underprotected online
Kids need more structured activities after school
Kids spend too little time on educational screens
Parents should monitor every online interaction
questions.why: The overview contrasts a play-based childhood with phone-based life.

questions.q: At what age does Haidt say social media should begin?
a: Sixteen
Twelve
Fourteen
Eighteen
questions.why: Lesson 2 sets sixteen, while phones should wait until high school.

questions.q: What does the summary say unsupervised play provides?
a: Social skills and self-reliance built through small failures
A safer alternative to outdoor sports
Structure that adults should carefully design
Benefits that appear only after age fourteen
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares setbacks to germs that strengthen the immune system.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the six spiritual practices?
a: Finding awe in nature
Keeping a private gratitude journal
Tracking your daily screen time
Joining a competitive sports league
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists shared sacredness, embodiment, stillness, self-transcendence, forgiveness and awe.
